title: Agent Context Memory: A Governance-First Specification for AI Agent Context Memory
description:
What this is. A specification for how AI-assisted work is kept organised in one shared memory (Shared Agent Context Memory, SACM), so that humans can audit it and stay responsible for the result. The same model serves one person and an organisation: a person working alone is a team of one.

The contribution. SACM recognizes that agent memory is fundamentally an authorization problem and applies established access control and audit-log patterns to this domain. The main proposal is the Mandate Gate: a pre-work mandate, confirmed by the principal, must exist in the agent's memory before work is a governed interval. Prior memory models (MemGPT, CoALA, Generative Agents) treat memory as a working resource the agent draws from during work. SACM treats memory as a precondition.

Core structure. Three memory tiers organized by trust level: Intent (principal-confirmed mandate), Trace (agent records, append-only) and Evidence (captured separately from the agent). Memory lives in a repository of its own and is bound to repositories of work by identity; scopes follow one rule (a folder holding a mandate, a learning file and records); shared recording uses one file per record. 23 numbered requirements each have a specified check; every one is Proposed.

Relationship to PEA. SACM implements the Principles of Earned Autonomy (PEA) for the context memory design problem: PEA is the theory, and its principles are SACM's one dependency. SACM stands on its own and can be implemented without the PEA skills.

Claims. The specification claims no implementation conformance: every requirement is Proposed. It acknowledges RBAC/MAC and audit-log principles and cites CoALA (arXiv:2309.02427), Generative Agents (arXiv:2304.03442) and MemGPT (arXiv:2310.08560).

Relationship to AII. SACM states the memory structure that the agency-preservation boundary condition of Augmented Individual Intelligence (AII) would need.

Read in this order. README.md (overview), then SPEC.md (the full specification).
